excerpt: BA (Hons) in Communications and Media Production Course Overview Are You Curious by Nature and Passionate About Uncovering and Sharing Stories? This BA (Hons) in Communications and Media Production is a full-time, three-year programme that aims to give students a foundation in an array of communications platforms, including social and digital media, photography, radio, investigative journalism, TV and video. The programme is perfect for students passionate about telling the stories that matter. Intake Dates - Dublin - Full-Time - September 2026 - Dublin - Full-Time - February 2027 Why Study Communications and Media Production at Griffith College Dublin? The communications industry is fast-paced, dynamic, and expanding rapidly in today’s digital age. Griffith College’s BA (Hons) in Communications and Media Production is a full-time, three-year degree designed to equip students with both the theoretical knowledge and practical skills required to thrive in this evolving field. Located in the heart of Dublin, this programme offers hands-on experience across a range of traditional and modern media platforms, including journalism, social and digital media, radio, photography, video, and television production. Key Benefits of the Programme: - Gain Real-World Media Experience: Develop practical skills by working across print (newspaper), broadcast (TV and radio), and digital platforms (social media, mobile journalism, and more). - Build a Strong Theoretical Foundation: Understand the principles of media theory, communication strategy, and media production techniques. - Create a Professional Portfolio: Contribute to Griffith’s in-house magazine, digital media hub. - Tailor Your Career Path: Choose from four specialist streams in Years 2 and 3 to focus on a preferred area of media. - Access Industry-Standard Facilities: Train in fully equipped on-campus studios including a film and TV production suite, professional photography studio, and a dedicated radio broadcasting space. - Professional Recognition: Qualify for a National Union of Journalists (NUJ) press pass, enhancing your professional credentials. - Progression Opportunities: Graduates can advance to one of Griffith College’s three specialist master’s degrees in media and digital communications. FAQs Students will gain hands-on experience across various media platforms, including social and digital media, photography, radio, investigative journalism, TV, and video production. The program emphasises project-based learning, allowing students to build an industry-standard portfolio. The program runs for three years full-time. In second and third year, students can choose specialised streams, allowing them to tailor their degree to their career interests. Graduates can enter careers in broadcasting, digital content creation, PR, journalism, and more or progress to one of Griffith College’s specialist master’s programs in media and digital communications. Related Courses Related Articles Course Details In first year, all students take the same core modules. In second year, students choose to either continue their study in Stream A (journalistic media) or Stream B (visual media). In third year, students choose three electives suited to their stream to accompany their mandatory modules. They may also choose from the common electives list.
